branch_network.notes: Present in all 48 contiguous states plus DC; no branches in Alaska or Hawaii

regions.name: Northeast
risk_factors: High commercial real estate exposure in NYC
High cost of living impacting consumer credit
regions.notes: Strongest region - includes NYC headquarters and legacy Chemical Bank/Chase Manhattan markets. #1 in deposits in New York. Recent expansion in Boston, Philadelphia, DC metro.

regions.name: Southeast
regions.notes: High-growth region. Florida is 3rd largest state by branch count (473 branches). Doubling presence in Carolinas to 45+ branches by 2027. Miami office expansion underway. Strong in Charlotte NC.

regions.name: Midwest
regions.notes: Legacy Bank One territory. Illinois is 5th largest state (318 branches). Strong in Chicago (#1 in deposits), Ohio (265 branches). Expanding in Iowa with 25 new branches planned by 2030. #1 in SBA lending in Illinois and Indiana.

regions.name: West
risk_factors: Drought and water scarcity (CA, NV, AZ, NM)
Commercial real estate overexposure in tech hubs
regions.notes: Largest region by branches. California is #1 state with 862-974 branches (sources vary). Strong in San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego. Washington Mutual acquisition (2008) expanded Pacific Northwest presence. #1 in SBA lending in Arizona.

regions.name: Southwest/South Central
risk_factors: Oil price volatility impact on business customers
regions.notes: Texas is 3rd largest state by branches (476-592 branches depending on source). #1 in deposits in Houston. #1 in SBA lending in Dallas-Fort Worth, Houston, and San Antonio. Growing Hispanic/Latino small business market.

concentration_metrics.notes: HHI below 1000 indicates high diversification. No single region exceeds 30%. Presence in 48 states provides strong geographic risk mitigation.

market_share_by_deposits.notes: Largest bank in US by deposits. Lead over Bank of America (11.0%) is narrow.

competitive_position.geographic_advantage: Only major bank with presence in all 48 contiguous states
competitive_position.expansion_vs_peers: Counter-trend: expanding branches while most banks consolidate

business_customer_profile.commercial_focus: Expanding affluent/wealth management centers in key metros

tech_sector.risk: Tech downturn could impact CRE and business lending

methodology.branch_counts: Based on Bank Branch Locator database and Chase official announcements (2024-2025)
methodology.regional_allocation: Estimated based on branch distribution, economic activity, and stated expansion priorities
methodology.business_counts: Estimated from 7M total business customers distributed proportionally by branch count and regional economic activity
methodology.deposit_share: Regional estimates based on branch distribution and known market share in key metros (NYC, Chicago, Houston)
methodology.market_share: Regional estimates based on FDIC data and announced market positions in key states
methodology.hhi_calculation: Sum of squared market shares by state for top 10 states
methodology.disaster_risk: Based on FEMA flood maps, USGS seismic zones, wildfire risk maps, and tornado climatology

data_quality_notes: Branch counts vary by source (4,700-5,100 range) due to different reporting dates and ongoing openings/closures
California branch count ranges from 862-974 depending on source and date
Business customer counts by region are estimates based on proportional distribution
Regional deposit share estimated from branch distribution and known metro market positions
Natural disaster exposure based on geographic location of branches, not actual risk-adjusted exposure
HHI index calculated using top 10 states only, not all 48 states
